conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that regular intake of vitamin C does not prevent common colds in the general population, directly rejecting the claim despite noting niche exceptions for extreme physical stress and small reductions in duration.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
### Conclusion
**No**, regular intake of vitamin C does not prevent common colds in the general population, though it can reduce cold risk for individuals under extreme physical stress and modestly shorten cold duration.

### Evidence
* **General Population:** A Cochrane systematic review of community trials involving 10,708 participants found a pooled risk ratio of 0.97, indicating that daily vitamin C does not significantly reduce cold incidence (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD000980_vitamin-c-preventing-and-treating-common-cold). Both the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements and the Mayo Clinic confirm that routine prophylactic vitamin C supplementation fails to prevent colds in the general public (https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminC-HealthProfessional/, https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements-vitamin-c/art-20363932).
* **Extreme Physical Stress:** In a subgroup exposed to short periods of severe physical exertion (such as marathon runners, skiers, and subarctic soldiers), daily vitamin C halved the risk of catching a cold (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD000980_vitamin-c-preventing-and-treating-common-cold).
* **Duration:** Although daily supplementation does not block infection for most people, evidence demonstrates it modestly reduces cold duration by about 8% to 10% (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279544/).

### Sources
- Cochrane Review: https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD000980_vitamin-c-preventing-and-treating-common-cold
- NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminC-HealthProfessional/
- Mayo Clinic: https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements-vitamin-c/art-20363932
- NCBI Bookshelf: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279544/
